overview.description: Hundred and Ten (110) is the bidding version of the Irish national game 'Twenty-Five' (Spoil Five). It is a strategic trick-taking game where players bid to score up to 110 points in a single deal. It is known for its peculiar card rankings (where red and black suits rank differently) and its aggressive bidding system.

history.origins: Derived from the 17th-century game 'Maw' and the classic 'Spoil Five'. The bidding variant '110' emerged in the 19th century as a way to add competitive depth to the social game of 'Twenty-Five'.
timeline: 1600s: Maw and Spoil Five are popular in the British Isles.
1800s: Bidding rules for 25/45/110 are established in rural Ireland.
Present: Remains a core social game in Irish pubs and households.
history.evolution: The game evolved by adding a precise scoring system (5 points per trick, 10 for the best trump) and escalating bids (up to the full 110).
history.cultural: Regarded as a key piece of Irish heritage; often played in organized 'drives' or tournaments.

setup.players: Usually 3 to 6 players as individuals, or 4/6 in partnerships.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. **Important**: Rankings vary by color and trump status.

rules.objective: Be the first player or team to reach 110 points across multiple deals.
rules.gameplay:
1. Must follow suit. If you can't, you can trump or discard.
2. **Renege**: A player can 'renege' (fail to follow suit) with one of the top three trumps (5, J, A of Hearts) unless a higher one is led.
keyRules: Follow the legal action constraints defined for Hundred and Ten.
Round outcome is resolved by the scoring method: Each trick is 5 points.
Winning condition: Be the first player or team to reach 110 points across multiple deals.

strategy.basic: If you hold the 5 of Trumps, you are guaranteed one trick. Use it to kill the opponent's King or Jack. Don't bid high without at least two of the top three trumps.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Spoil': If you aren't the bidder, your job is to prevent the bidder from getting their tricks. Play defensively and cover their leads.
strategy.advanced: Jinking assessment: Only bid a Jink if you have the 5 and at least 3 other high trumps. A single 'lucky' lead from an opponent can kill a Jink bid.
tips: Remember the ranking: 'Highest in Red, Lowest in Black' for number cards.
The Ace of Hearts is ALWAYS a trump.

difficulty.medium: Reasonable bidding; manages top-three trumps correctly.

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck with four suits and thirteen ranks per suit; some variants use one or two jokers. Hundred and Ten (110) is a point-trick game where the first side to reach 110 points wins the round or game.
engine.suitDescription: The four French suits (hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades) each contain thirteen cards. One suit is typically trump each round; following suit and trump rules determine trick winner and point collection.
engine.rankDescription: Standard ranks Ace through 2; point values are assigned to certain cards (e.g. Tens, Aces, Kings). The total of card points in the deck is usually 110 or a multiple; first to 110 (or agreed target) wins.
